title: VaultSecret — shared definition for vault secret material
description:
Schema for the cleartext secret payload of a vault entry. Documents the shape both sides of a vault/release/0.1 transfer code-generate against. The secret payload is NEVER transmitted as plaintext JSON on the wire: vault/release/0.1 returns it inside an HPKE-sealed envelope (see SealedSecret in the vault/release payload schema). This shared schema is the authoritative description of the bytes inside that envelope.

Sensitive fields (`password`, `privateKey`, `refreshToken`, `secureNotes`, etc.) MUST be zeroised by consumers as soon as their use is complete. Consumers MUST NOT log, persist beyond cache lifetime, or transmit the cleartext outside the release-time scope.

Discriminated by `kind`, which mirrors VaultEntry.secretKind on the metadata side. The `kind` value MUST equal the metadata view's `secretKind` for the same entry.

loginConfig.description: Optional driver config for `vault/proxy-login/0.1` against a Password-kind entry. When present, the maintainer performs an HTTP POST against the configured endpoint with the entry's `username` + `password` and returns the resulting Set-Cookie headers in the SessionBlob (`cookies[]`). When absent, the maintainer rejects proxy-login for this entry with `not_proxyable` — the consumer falls back to vault/release for a browser-fill flow. Drivers other than HTTP POST (e.g. OAuth refresh, DIDComm) live on their own secret kinds; this struct is HTTP-POST-only.

secureNotes.description: Sensitive notes (security questions, account recovery context). Distinct from `notes` on the metadata view — `notes` is non-sensitive, this is.

PasswordLoginConfig.title: PasswordLoginConfig
PasswordLoginConfig.description: How the maintainer should POST this entry's username + password to the third party during a vault/proxy-login/0.1 call. Modeled to cover the two formats consumer login APIs almost always use (JSON body, URL-encoded form body) plus the field-name flexibility most sites need. Sites that demand a CSRF token fetched in a separate round-trip, multi-step MFA prompts, or anti-bot challenges are out of scope here — those need a richer driver (future spec).

loginUrl.description: Absolute URL the maintainer POSTs the credentials to. MUST be `https://` for any non-loopback target — maintainers MUST reject `http://` URLs outside the localhost loopback (defense against credential leakage on transit). The host of this URL also constrains which Set-Cookie domains the maintainer is willing to accept on the response (cookies with a domain unrelated to the loginUrl's host SHOULD be discarded — see `vault/_shared/0.1/session-blob#/$defs/CookieJarEntry.domain`).

format.description: Wire format for the request body. `json`: `Content-Type: application/json`, body is `{"<usernameField>": ..., "<passwordField>": ..., ...extraFields}`. `form-urlencoded`: `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, body is the same fields URL-encoded.

usernameField.description: Field name carrying the username in the request body. Common alternatives: `email`, `login`, `userId`.

passwordField.description: Field name carrying the password in the request body.

totpField.description: Optional field name carrying the TOTP code in the request body. When set AND the entry's `totp` is populated, the maintainer computes the current 6-digit code and includes it in the request alongside username + password. Omit for sites that prompt for TOTP in a separate round-trip (out of scope here).

extraFields.description: Optional constant field/value pairs the maintainer MUST include in the request body alongside the credentials. Use for fixed selectors like `{"grantType": "password"}` or feature toggles the site expects. Values are constants — anything dynamic (CSRF tokens, request ids) is out of scope and needs a richer driver.

successStatus.description: HTTP status codes the maintainer treats as login success. Default `[200, 204]`. A response status outside this list MUST cause the maintainer to reject the proxy-login with `credential_rejected` (when 4xx) or `target_unreachable` (when 5xx).

privateKey.description: Base64url-encoded private key bytes (algorithm implied by `algorithm`).

provider.description: Provider identifier ("google", "github", or a maintainer-defined string for less-common providers).

signingKeyId.description: Maintainer-internal identifier for the signing key (the key itself is held by the VTA; this is a pointer).

headerName.description: Name of the HTTP header to carry the token in. Most APIs use "Authorization" with a "Bearer " prefix; some use "X-Api-Key" or similar.

headerPrefix.description: String to prepend to the token when forming the header value.

privateKey.description: PEM-encoded private key (OpenSSH or PKCS#8 format).

passphrase.description: Optional passphrase if the private key is itself encrypted.

name.description: Field label (also exposed in metadata view as `customFieldNames`).

hidden.description: When true, consumers SHOULD render the value as masked (dotted) by default and require an explicit reveal action.

kind.description: Hint for the consumer UI's rendering.
